Cavalry is the army, mailed lancers and horse archers on stirrups, and Turkish archers are prized. The chariot is ancient history. - **Mechanical artillery (torsion catapult, trebuchet)** [`torsion_artillery_trebuchet`](https://blueprintsfromtomorrow.com/techtree/generated/tech/torsion_artillery_trebuchet.md) — K4, use correct, make medium, accept high. Traction trebuchets (manjaniq) pulled by crews, and light 'arrada, shelled Baghdad's houses in 812–813. The counterweight trebuchet is unknown; torsion engines survive in Greek books.
- **Oared war galley and ram tactics** [`oared_galley_ram`](https://blueprintsfromtomorrow.com/techtree/generated/tech/oared_galley_ram.md) — K3, use partial, make medium, accept medium. Fleets of Syria and Egypt row galleys that fight by boarding, not ramming; in 827 Andalusian exiles take Crete and the Aghlabids invade Sicily. On the Tigris, armed river craft fought in the siege.

Naphtha from Iraqi seeps is thrown in pots or on arrows by specialist naphtha men (naffatun). The Byzantine siphon that sprays burning oil from ships is a guarded secret. Elsewhere: Constantinople, Greek fire siphons.

The trench (khandaq) is part of sacred history (Medina, 627); armies ditch their camps and Baghdad's defenders dug in during the siege. Against Babak's mountain strongholds it will need patience.

Saltpetre is unknown to Arab chemists until the 13th century, though nitre crusts form on old mud walls and stables. Sulphur and charcoal are at hand. In China alchemists are just finding the mixture dangerous. Elsewhere: Tang China, Daoist alchemists' saltpetre-sulphur mixtures.
